Package io.mavlink4j.transport

Interface SerialChannel

All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable
public interface SerialChannel extends AutoCloseable
The byte-level seam SerialLink polls/writes through. Public so a host can plug in any serial backend and a test can fake a port without loading a native library, exactly like MavlinkLink itself lets a test fake a whole link.

Implementer contract: read(byte[], int) is called from one reader thread and must never block past its timeout; write(byte[], int, int) may be called from several threads and must be safe for that (or be serialized by the caller's SerialLink); close() is idempotent and unblocks a pending read.

Not a bare InputStream/OutputStream pair: jSerialComm has no Socket.setSoTimeout-equivalent on the stream it hands back — the read timeout is a property of the underlying SerialPort object, set via setComPortTimeouts, not of any one read call. read(byte[], int) threads the timeout through explicitly instead, so SerialLink.poll(java.time.Duration) can honor a fresh Duration on every call the same way TcpClientLink#poll does with Socket#setSoTimeout.

  • Method Details

    • portDescriptor

      String portDescriptor()
      The stable port name this channel talks to, e.g. "/dev/ttyUSB0" or "COM3".

    • read

      int read(byte[] buffer, int timeoutMillis) throws IOException
      Reads up to buffer.length bytes, waiting at most timeoutMillis for at least one to arrive.
      Returns:
      the number of bytes read, 0 on timeout with nothing available (jSerialComm's semi-blocking read contract — never blocks past timeoutMillis), or a negative value if the underlying port has reached end-of-stream (unplugged mid-read)
      Throws:
      IOException
